item.title: Kudjip hospital faces shutdown over K5.7 million funding gap
item.description: Thousands of patients across Jiwaka and the Upper Highlands region could face serious disruption to essential healthcare services as Nazarene General Hospital at Kudjip battles a financial crisis threatening its continued operations. The hospital has temporarily averted closure following emergency funding assistance, but its management warns that the reprieve may be short-lived unless the National
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of patients across Jiwaka and the Upper Highlands region could face serious disruption to essential healthcare services as Nazarene General Hospital at Kudjip battles a financial crisis threatening its continued operations.

The hospital has temporarily averted closure following emergency funding assistance, but its management warns that the reprieve may be short-lived unless the National Government urgently releases an additional K5.7 million.

The Level Five provincial referral hospital was preparing to close its outpatient, accident and emergency, and labour and delivery services on November 2 due to a severe funding crisis.

However, emergency assistance from the Christian Health Services and the Jiwaka Provincial Health Authority has bought the hospital more time to continue providing essential medical services.

Jiwaka Provincial Health Authority (JPHA) Board Chairman Paulus Ain says the emergency funding is only temporary relief, with the hospital still facing a significant financial shortfall.

" The emergency assistance by CHS and JPHA would only take the hospital operations through a month or two, but the hospital still will need the funding shortfall to take it through to the next fiscal year."

According to the joint statement issued by the hospital management and the Jiwaka Provincial Health Authority, the facility received K1.5 million from Christian Health Services and K500,000 from the Jiwaka Provincial Health Authority.

Ain also says its total funding gap for this financial year stands at approximately K12.8 million, covering essential operational costs, medical supplies, facility maintenance, utilities, staff housing rentals and outstanding staff allowances.

Hospital Chief Executive Officer Ambassador Paulias Korni stress the emergency assistance has provided temporary breathing space, but the underlying financial crisis remains unresolved.

" We would like to thank the CHS and the JPHA to come on board in this crucial tome of the hospital with the K2 million assistance.

"This does not mean the planned shutdown of the hospital will not eventually, unless the needed funding is made available then the hospital does not have a choice but to close its operations," says Ambassador Korni.

The JPHA board and management as well as the Kudjip Nazarene Hospital is now appealing to the Prime Minister to direct the Department of Treasury to release a further K5.7 million in emergency funding to sustain services for the remainder of the year.

"We are now making an urgent call to the relevant responsible ministries to release the warrant and make available the K5.7 million needed for the continued operations of Kudjip Hospital.

"People's lives are at stake and the funds needed will not benefit our pockets rather the very people that makes the government. Because Jiwaka is yet to have a Provincial Hospital of its own, for now the services provided at the Kudjip Hospital must be taken seriously by the government," stressed Chairman Ain.

The hospital warns that without further government intervention, the threat of an indefinite shutdown remains, putting essential healthcare services for the people of Jiwaka and the Upper Highlands region at risk.

The requested funding is needed to maintain cash flow for essential medical supplies, utilities and staff obligations while longer-term budget issues are addressed.

And while the strong call for the national government as well as call for local parliamentarians of Jiwaka to intervene, this is to ensure patients continue receiving uninterrupted medical care at Kudjip Nazarene Hospital.

item.title: Madang gets new police chief
item.description: Madang police has welcomed a new Provincial Police Commander (PPC) amidst confusion. The sudden change came as a surprise to both police officers and members of the general public in the province who are now questioning the motive behind the shift, especially when the country is nearing the 2027 National General Election.
item.content:encoded:
Madang police has welcomed a new Provincial Police Commander (PPC) amidst confusion.

The sudden change came as a surprise to both police officers and members of the general public in the province who are now questioning the motive behind the shift, especially when the country is nearing the 2027 National General Election.

According to recent media reports from the Police Commissioner, David Manning, the changes are part of the ongoing evolution in the RPNGC, which are essential to meet the operational requirements and improved discipline, and effective policing across the country.

A handover/ takeover quarter parade was held this morning at the provincial police headquarters at Jomba Police Station as part of the farewell formalities for Mr Baim and to welcome the new PPC, Chief Inspector Vakaruru Uraia.

Chief Inspector Uraia is a retired police officer from Fiji who has served the New Zealand police force for 35 years.

He has a background in criminal investigation.

His predecessor, Superintendent Robert Baim, who served as Madang's top cop for three years since 2023, said he was grateful to be handing over the command to Uraia.

However, prior to that, Baim provided a detailed verbal rundown of the overall police operations in Madang Province.

He told the new PPC that Madang is a big command with 250 plus policemen and women, more than 200 reservists, and tasking is a bit difficult; especially with limited resources.

" I am more than happy to hand over the command to you. I am also grateful you came to serve my province. I am a local man from Madang, and I am only a phone call away if you need my help or any advice.

" Don't take advice from junior officers. Seek advice from your sectional heads. I don't take advice from the junior officers. They will talk nicely in front of you, and then they backstab you.

" Stick to yourself, trust your section heads, and maintain your command," Baim said.

Mr Baim also highlighted the challenges that Madang police face in their everyday quest to maintain law and order.

Chief amongst them is the shortage of manpower, which has seen Madang engaging more than 200 reservists throughout the province who work tirelessly but are not on the payroll.

" We liaise with the Madang Provincial Government for their allowances.The provincial government has been very good in assisting us, however; their allowances for last year are yet to be paid.

" The Madang Government's has been very supportive to Madang police in the last three years, and I highly appreciate the working collaboration," Baim said.

He added that logistics is also a major hindrance to effective policing in the province, but this does not stop the officers from performing their duties.

Mr Baim became emotional whilst highlighting the willingness of officers to work extra time without getting paid any allowances.

" We have very hard-working police officers. They work tirelessly. They don't claim overtime.They have the heart to serve.

" They need good leadership. They need very strong leadership. Madang is one of the province that needs strong leadership in command and control.

" And these hard-working men, the warriors I call them. They will be in the forefront.

" I have taken back Madang. Madang is now safe and peaceful unlike before when it was referred to as the "murder capital," Mr Baim said.

Meanwhile, Chief Inspector Uraia thanked the outgoing PPC for the insights provided on the challenges of leadership, emphasising that he is not here to just take over from him, rather to carry on the passion and services that he has provided for Madang.

As he takes on the baton from Baim, he is mindful of the chain of command.

" Coming from an investigative background, I am very strict with standards, and that's what I intend to do. I will be speaking with the sectional heads so we become good role models.

" As I take on the baton from Mr Baim, I would also to wish him all the best in the next phase of his journey, " Uraia said.

Whilst all other formalities of the handover/ takeover were completed today, the new PPC has asked that he review the contents of the HOTO instruments before he can sign in the next one or two days.

The handover/ takeover was witnessed by the Acting ACP for the Northern Command, Samson Siguyaru, a handful of senior government officers, members of the general public and the media.

item.title: Community leader calls for urgent action on Sepik-highway lawlessness
item.description: Former two-term Member of Parliament for Maprik, businessman, and community leader John Simon has issued an urgent plea to East Sepik leaders to address the deteriorating law and order situation crippling the province’s key economic arteries. Speaking on behalf of the business community, PMV operators, and the people of Maprik, Wosera Gawi, Ambunti Drekikier, Yangoru Saussia, and Nuku and Lumi, Mr
item.content:encoded:
Former two-term Member of Parliament for Maprik, businessman, and community leader John Simon has issued an urgent plea to East Sepik leaders to address the deteriorating law and order situation crippling the province’s key economic arteries.

Speaking on behalf of the business community, PMV operators, and the people of Maprik, Wosera Gawi, Ambunti Drekikier, Yangoru Saussia, and Nuku and Lumi, Mr. Simon expressed deep concern over the continuous armed hold-ups and brutal violence targeted at public transport providers and travelers along the Sepik Highway.

The call follows a series of terrifying security incidents, including the recent injuring of a Public Motor Vehicle (PMV) driver at Nagam Bridge and the tragic killing of a PMV owner and businessman at Yangisaku. The lawlessness escalated further on Wednesday morning when two 25-seater PMV buses were held up by criminals at the Boem Sara area of Yangoru.

"As a businessman with investments in both Maprik and Wewak, I am seeing firsthand how these unchecked criminal activities are destroying lives, livelihoods, and the local economy," Simon said.

"Our PMV drivers and owners are providing an essential public service, yet they are being hunted, robbed, and killed on our highways. Families are living in fear, and businesses are struggling to survive under the constant threat of armed violence.

With the current challenges of El Niño weather conditions, these threats are further increased. I also feel unsafe traveling up and down the highway myself."

Simon emphasized that Maprik currently lacks a direct voice to demand immediate state intervention following the untimely passing of its sitting Member of Parliament, the late Libert Kapris, over the weekend.

"Maprik has lost its representative and its voice in the National Parliament. Because our district cannot formally speak on this issue during this time of mourning, I am stepping forward to speak on behalf of our people and our neighboring communities and districts who rely entirely on the safety of the Sepik Highway for travel and business."

Simon appeals to the political leadership of East Sepik Province, calling on Governor Allan Bird, Yangoru-Saussia MP Richard Maru, Wosera Gawi MP Joseph Yopyyopy, Ambunti-Dreikikier MP Johnson Wapunai, Angoram MP Salio Waipo, as well as Wewak MP Stanley Samban to urgently come together and find solutions to restore safety before the festive periods.

"I am calling on our Governor and our district leaders to put a stop to these continuous hold-ups and killings. Our leaders must not concentrate too much on national political issues at the expense of the safety of our mothers, fathers, and children on the ground. National politics will not save the lives of our people being terrorized either on the Wewak, Yangoru Saussia, Angoram, Maprik, Wosera Gawi, Ambunti Drekikier, or Nuku and Lumi sections of the highway."

He is also calling on the Marape-Rosso Government, as well as the Police Minister to take this matter seriously, because the Sepik Highway is an important economic route for PNG.

He is also calling on the police hierarchy in Port Moresby to investigate why East Sepik police could not curb this lawlessness while more lives are being lost every week. Mr. Simon questioned whether the systemic failure stems from funding constraints, manpower shortages, logistics issues, or a severe lack of command and control within the province’s police force.

"We need permanent police checkpoints, increased highway patrols, and aggressive intelligence-led operations to flush out these criminals. I urge our leaders to redirect their focus back home, work together across district lines, and deliver the security that the people of East Sepik rightfully deserve."

Simon also used this opportunity to convey his, his family's, his clan's, and the Malba community's heartfelt condolences to the Kapris family, their relatives, and the Supari, Iwam, Ami and the Albiges communities in the Albiges Mamblep LLG, as well as the people of Maprik, on the passing of their son, brother, uncle, nephew, and grandchild, the late Libert Kapris.

"Though we were political opponents in the 2024 by-election, Libert will always remain as my son. I and my family and tribe are greatly saddened that Maprik has lost such a young leader at this time," Simon concluded.

item.title: Air Niugini urges caution, after fire incident at the international airport
item.description: Air Niugini has issued an urgent safety warning to passengers regarding the handling, charging, and transport of lithium battery-powered devices, following a fire incident at the Jacksons International Airport in Port Moresby. The national flag carrier’s Chief Executive Officer, Alan Milne, issued the directive, after a charging power bank, caused a minor electrical fire and smoke incident, at the
item.content:encoded:
Air Niugini has issued an urgent safety warning to passengers regarding the handling, charging, and transport of lithium battery-powered devices, following a fire incident at the Jacksons International Airport in Port Moresby.

The national flag carrier’s Chief Executive Officer, Alan Milne, issued the directive, after a charging power bank, caused a minor electrical fire and smoke incident, at the Domestic Kumul Club Lounge on Saturday, October 24.

While lounge members and staff quickly contained the fire without any reported injuries, the airline is using the incident to remind travelers of the severe risks associated with lithium batteries.

In an official statement, Mr. Milne highlighted that everyday items like mobile phones, laptops, tablets, and power banks are classified as "hidden dangerous goods" that can pose catastrophic risks to passengers, property, and aircraft safety.

The airline warned that these devices become high-risk fire hazards if the batteries are, damaged or faulty, exposed to excessive heat, swollen, and charged using uncertified or incompatible equipment.

To prevent future incidents, Air Niugini is urging all customers to strictly; use only manufacturer-approved chargers and cables, immediately stop using and traveling with batteries that appear swollen or damage, never leave devices unattended while they are charging, and always answer all dangerous goods safety questions truthfully, during check in.

"Lithium battery-powered devices have become an essential part of daily life, but they must be used and handled responsibly," Milne said.

He reiterated that safety remains Air Niugini's highest priority, both on the ground and in the air, and the airline will continue to run dangerous goods awareness and training programs for its staff and external cargo partners, to strengthen safety measures across its network.

item.title: Supreme court returns to Kavieng after 30 years
item.description: The return of Papua New Guinea’s Supreme Court to Kavieng after approximately 30 years has marked a significant milestone for access to justice in New Ireland Province, with Chief Justice Sir Gibbs Salika confirming that a full-time resident judge will be appointed to the province in 2027. The confirmation came during the ceremonial opening of the Supreme Court premises in Kavieng, attended by sen
item.content:encoded:
The return of Papua New Guinea’s Supreme Court to Kavieng after approximately 30 years has marked a significant milestone for access to justice in New Ireland Province, with Chief Justice Sir Gibbs Salika confirming that a full-time resident judge will be appointed to the province in 2027.

The confirmation came during the ceremonial opening of the Supreme Court premises in Kavieng, attended by senior judicial officers, government representatives and provincial leaders ahead of the scheduled commencement of the five-men bench.

New Ireland Governor Byron Chan welcomed the Court’s presence, describing it as an important step towards bringing justice closer to the people.

Governor Chan said the presence of the country’s highest court would allow New Ireland residents to pursue their legal rights and seek interpretation of the law locally. He also raised concerns over killings, the burning of businesses and other law-and-order issues, expressing hope that the Court’s presence would strengthen public confidence in the justice system.

Acting Deputy Chief Justice Penuel Mogish highlighted the historical significance of the occasion, recalling that the Supreme Court had previously sat in Kavieng around 1986.

Justice Mogish said people from New Ireland and Manus had faced the burden of travelling to Port Moresby for court proceedings. He appealed for a full-time resident judge in Kavieng to reduce travel costs and delays and improve the management of criminal and civil cases.

Responding to Justice Mogish’s appeal, Chief Justice Sir Gibbs Salika confirmed that a full-time resident judge would be appointed to Kavieng in 2027, restoring a permanent judicial presence in New Ireland.

“We intend to pick it up again next year,” Sir Gibbs said, referring to the previous arrangement of having a judge based in Kavieng.

The Chief Justice also reflected on his first visit to Kavieng in 1980 as a young lawyer, recalling that court facilities were limited to a single courthouse with basic office services.

He acknowledged the improvements made to the Kavieng court premises and said the Judiciary would continue upgrading facilities to meet the country’s growing legal needs.

Sir Gibbs further expressed confidence in Papua New Guinea’s lawyers and judges, stressing the importance of training more legal professionals to strengthen the country’s justice institutions and meet increasing demands for legal services.

The ceremonial opening began with a guard of honour and parade march, followed by a ribbon-cutting ceremony to officially open the Supreme Court premises.

The scheduled five-men bench- sitting and the confirmed appointment of a resident judge in 2027 will mark important developments in efforts to strengthen judicial services and improve access to justice for the people of New Ireland Province.

item.title: National narcotics bureau plans Morobe office
item.description: The National Narcotics Bureau is working to establish a provincial coordination office in Morobe to strengthen drug awareness and improve coordination with communities and government agencies. Director General Kiria Kotange says a two-week training and awareness program is underway in Morobe to prepare community representatives to become narcotics ambassadors.
item.content:encoded:
The National Narcotics Bureau is working to establish a provincial coordination office in Morobe to strengthen drug awareness and improve coordination with communities and government agencies.

Director General Kiria Kotange says a two-week training and awareness program is underway in Morobe to prepare community representatives to become narcotics ambassadors.

The program includes one week of training followed by a week of community awareness activities involving youth, women, public servants and law enforcement personnel nominated by the Morobe Provincial Administration in consultation with partner agencies.

“Our aim is to bring more awareness into the communities, to the provinces, to make people aware of the drugs being used in our country,” Kotange says.

He says the program supports the implementation of a Memorandum of Understanding signed between the Bureau and the Morobe Provincial Administration in May this year to establish a narcotics coordination office in the province.

Morobe is part of the Bureau’s broader plan to expand its presence beyond the national headquarters and improve its reach across Papua New Guinea.

Kotange says marijuana remains a major concern, while other drugs, including methamphetamine and cocaine, also pose challenges.

He says the Bureau focuses on drug awareness, coordination and reporting, while police are responsible for arrests and law enforcement.

“The enforcement power lies with the police. The arresting power is done by the police,” he says.

Deputy Director for Policy and Operations Robert Naipat says inadequate government funding remains a major obstacle to extending the Bureau’s programs across the country’s 22 provinces.

The Bureau currently operates from its national headquarters and has recently established an office in Bougainville, with Morobe expected to be the next province to receive a coordination office.

“Unfortunately, the government does not allocate enough budget to the National Narcotics Bureau, so that is an impediment that prevents the Bureau from reaching out to all the provinces in the country,” Naipat says.

Both officials are calling for stronger cooperation between government agencies, businesses, community organisations and the public, particularly young people, to address drug abuse.

The proposed Morobe office is expected to strengthen provincial coordination and support ongoing efforts to educate communities about drug use and its impacts.

item.title: Twelve dead after robbery in Kimbe
item.description: Twelve suspects who robbed a retail outlet in Kimbe Town this morning were killed in a crossfire with police while they were attempting to flee in a getaway vehicle. Police Commissioner, David Manning in a press statement confirmed that while attempting to escape in the stolen vehicle, the getaway car overturned and rolled over resulting in the deaths of some of the suspects.
item.content:encoded:
Twelve suspects who robbed a retail outlet in Kimbe Town this morning were killed in a crossfire with police while they were attempting to flee in a getaway vehicle.

Police Commissioner, David Manning in a press statement confirmed that while attempting to escape in the stolen vehicle, the getaway car overturned and rolled over resulting in the deaths of some of the suspects.

According to the statement, the remaining suspects who were not seriously injured when the vehicle overturned, drew their weapons and opened fire on police leaving police officers with few options but to return fire.

The Commissioner clarified that police standing orders are clear in that when a criminal raises a weapon, they will be stopped.

Commissioner Manning confirmed that 12 gunmen died in the incident while one suspect, believed to be the ringleader survived and is now in police custody.

“Police officers recovered stolen currency, as well as a sizable quantity of weapons and ammunition from the vehicle,” he clarified.

Commissioner Manning says investigations into the incident are continuing and a report will be prepared for the Coroner.

Manning called on youths to turn away from crime lead productive lives.

“Our stance against criminal gangs is firm but there is still a way forward for young people who have been drawn into gang life. I call on them to turn away from violence, reconnect with their families and communities and choose a lawful and productive future,” he said.

Police Minister, John Pundari also commended the quick intervention by Kimbe police.

“I commend those police officers on the frontline in West New Britain Province who have confronted criminals involved in two-armed robberies over the past four days,

“This follows an event last Friday when a group of gunmen robbed a PMV near Kimbe and were confronted by a lone police officer. Following an exchange of gunfire, one gunman was killed while the remainder ran away into the bushes,” Minister Pundari said.

item.title: Three missing people return to PNG
item.description: The three people who went missing for 70 days, were finally repatriated from the Republic of Kiribati and returned to Papua New Guinea today. The safe repatriation of Horan Kapeatu, Francis-Mitchelle Tokiapron and Darrell Tokiapron who come from the Nissan Island in Bougainville, was supported by National Member for North Bougainville, Francesca Semoso and Regional Member, Peter Tsiamalili Jr.
item.content:encoded:
The three people who went missing for 70 days, were finally repatriated from the Republic of Kiribati and returned to Papua New Guinea today.

The safe repatriation of Horan Kapeatu, Francis-Mitchelle Tokiapron and Darrell Tokiapron who come from the Nissan Island in Bougainville, was supported by National Member for North Bougainville, Francesca Semoso and Regional Member, Peter Tsiamalili Jr.

The safe repatriation of these three survivors was led by two officials, Quentin Talingapua, Cordinator of ABG Directorate of Disaster & Emergency and Sylvester Vakore from the PNG Immigration and citizenship services authority.

According to one of the survivors, Francis-Mitchelle Tokiapron, they started drifting away from Nissan Island right after they had run out of fuel.

"On that day, fuel finished so we drifted on the sea towards Lihir Island," said Francis-Mitchelle.

He said while out at sea, the three of them had to survive on what little they had and had to drink salt water when they became thirsty.

"We ate fish, turtle and shark and drank the sea when were thirsty," he said.

Mitchelle also said they are very happy to be back home and look forward to seeing their families again.

Member for North Bougainville, Francesca Semoso, who was also present to welcome the three missing people, said she is very happy for their safe return.

"Thankyou to these three for not giving up. Your families are very excited and waiting for you at home,' said Semoso.

She also thanked the Marape-Rosso Government, Immigration Office here in PNG, Disaster Buka and the people of Kiribati for looking after the three PNG Nationals.

Semoso described the repatriation as a humanitarian obligation and urged the people of Papua New Guinea to take precaution while traveling by sea to avoid future incidents like this one.

"The money we used for the repatriation of these three people, was not an easy decision especially with the current El Nino. People were questioning why we had to spend this amount of money for this mission. Humanity is about people,' said Semoso.
